title: Spatial Item Factor Analysis
text: vignette, show use spifa package fit spatial multidimensional 2 parameter logistic model, used item response theory. Let YijY_{ij} binary response item jj individual ii. model can defined using auxiliary variable ZijZ_{ij} $$\begin{align}   {Y}_{ij}  & =   \left\lbrace   \begin{array}[2]{cc}     1 & \text{} ~ {Z}_{ij} > 0\\     0 & \text{otherwise}   \end{array}   \right.\\   {Z}_{ij} & = c_j + a_j^\intercal\theta_i + \epsilon_{ij},   ~~ \epsilon_{ij} \sim {N}(0, 1) \end{align}$$ vector latent abilities θi\theta_i modelled, spatial case, θi=Xi⊺B+w(si)+vi, \theta_i = X_i^\intercal B + w(s_i) + v_i, sum predictor effect (Xi⊺BX_i^\intercal B, XiX_i row predictors individual ii BB matrix effects), multivariate Gaussian process capturing spatial dependence (w(si)w(s_i), location sis_i), multivariate non-spatial term (viv_i), rather assumed independent across individuals.

title: Bayesian Spatial Item Factor Analysis
text: spifa fits spatial item factor analysis (IFA) models binary responses using full Bayesian inference (adaptive Metropolis-Hastings within Gibbs sampling), via auxiliary variables probit link function. latent factors modelled sum predictor effect, multivariate Gaussian process capturing spatial dependence, multivariate non-spatial term, spatially referenced constructs (e.g. food insecurity socio-economic index measured survey locations) can mapped predicted new locations. Standard exploratory confirmatory IFA supported particular cases, simply dropping spatial structure. package implements methodology described “Mapping food insecurity Brazilian Amazon using spatial item factor analysis model” (2025), published Annals Applied Statistics https://doi.org/10.1214/25-AOAS2072. addition core spatial item factor analysis model, spifa offers tools model diagnostics, visualization, summarizing results.

title: Bayesian Spatial Item Factor Analysis

code: library(spifa)  data(ipixuna) nfactors <- 3 nitems <- ncol(ipixuna$items)  # define a restriction for the discrimination A <- matrix(1, nitems, nfactors) A[c(1, 3, 5), 1] <- 0 A[c(2, 6, 9), 2] <- 0 A[c(4, 7, 10), 3] <- 0  # sampling from the posterior distribution samples <- spifa(items ~ 1, data = ipixuna, nfactors = nfactors, niter = 1000,   constraints = list(discrimination = A))  # visualize the easiness parameters (c) plot(samples, select = "c", burnin = 500)

title: Bayesian Spatial Item Factor Analysis — spifa
text: type model fitted determined automatically formula class data: one-sided right-hand side (items ~ 1) constraints$discrimination left unspecified gives exploratory IFA (EIFA) – default lower-triangular restriction discrimination applied automatically identifiability case, something user chooses (see constraints ). EIFA also never estimates correlation latent factors: stays fixed priors$corr$initial (identity default) whole fit – see priors . Supplying (typically theory-driven) restricted constraints$discrimination instead gives confirmatory IFA (CIFA); adding predictors right-hand side (e.g. items ~ x1) gives CIFA predictors; data sf object adds spatial Gaussian process latent factors, giving spatial IFA (SPIFA), without predictors. left-hand side formula must single symbol naming matrix-valued column data (nobs x nitems, one row per respondent, one column per binary item) — mechanism base R uses multivariate lm. Build (ordinary $<- assignment) survives matrix column rather flattened separate columns, e.g.: Parameter glossary. priors/constraints use descriptive names; fitted model's sampled output (seen via summary.spifa, plot_trace, friends) instead uses short internal names matching underlying model notation. two deliberately different vocabularies (configure vs. sampler produced) – table maps :

title: Summarise spifa Posterior Samples — summary.spifa
text: Computes posterior summary statistics every parameter fitted spifa object, via summarise_draws: mean, median, sd, mad, 2.5%/10%/50%/90%/97.5% quantiles, effective sample size (bulk tail), rhat. rhat computed via split-chain R-hat (Vehtari et al. 2021), splits chain half compares halves – remains meaningful convergence diagnostic even though spifa ever fits single chain.

title: Continue Sampling from the Posterior of a spifa Model — update.spifa
text: adaptive Metropolis-Hastings proposal tuning (residual correlation , spifa/spifa_pred, Gaussian process parameters) resumes wherever object's run left , rather restarting object's original adaptive settings – chain update() calls keeps refining proposal instead re-paying adaptation time. update() always uses standardize setting object originally fit (see spifa); argument . standardize's rescale still computed independently call, call's posterior draws, object object returned can end slightly different absolute scales even though represent continuous chain. Combine (e.g. rbind() as_draws_matrix form) want one continuous chain; fit standardize = FALSE first place want every continuation genuinely identical, unrescaled scale.
